expected.finding: **[P2]** `.github/workflows/revise-improvement-policy.yml`: checkout does not pin the default branch. A manual dispatch on a feature branch checks out that branch, so the proposed PR also includes its unrelated, unmerged commits. Restrict dispatches to `main` or explicitly checkout the default branch. Staging selected files does not exclude existing commits. See [checkout’s ref behavior](https://github.com/actions/checkout#usage).

**[P2]** `.github/workflows/revise-improvement-policy.yml`: PR deduplication only checks the SHA-specific branch. If another archive update lands while a revision PR remains open, the next run creates another proposal with the same policy version and parent. These competing proposals conflict in the policy, history, and measurements. Update or supersede the outstanding policy proposal before creating another.

**[P2]** `scripts/measure-policy-validity.py`, `collect_trace_evidence`: each search stops at 100 results, but those truncated results become absolute field counts without pagination or a truncation indicator. Frequent topics can collapse into identical counts, distorting Spearman agreement or making validity undefined and disabling its revision trigger. Collect all results or explicitly handle incomplete counts.

**[P2]** `scripts/render-rsi-dashboard.py`, `trigger_chart`: every revision and rollback marker uses `xs[-1]`, regardless of when it occurred. Subsequent archive updates move all historical changes to the newest round and stack their labels together, making the chart misrepresent when policy changes happened. Position markers using each history entry’s timestamp or recorded decision epoch.
